description: GEI Mapping, formerly Energy Web Atlas, is a commercial ESRI-based mapping platform from Global Energy Infrastructure that shows energy assets worldwide. It covers downstream refining, petrochemicals, gas processing and biofuels construction projects, global gas and oil pipelines, LNG facilities, hydrogen and carbon capture and storage. The provider states that asset locations are verified through satellite imagery, regulatory filings and operator validation, that each point or line links to capacity, ownership, status and technical specifications, and that the map is updated continuously with new projects, capacity changes and ownership transfers. Users can overlay layers, filter by capacity, owner, status, technology, feedstock, product slate and commissioning date, zoom from global to asset level, and export map images and CSV data with filters preserved. Access is online by subscription after a demo request; pricing and licence terms are not published, and sample maps show refining capacity, the North American pipeline network and Asia-Pacific LNG terminals. Coverage is global. Caveats: proprietary data with vendor-stated accuracy, not available for open reuse. Simulation uses are refinery, pipeline and LNG asset layers for exposure, supply disruption and capacity studies. Related records: data-ogim-oil-gas-infrastructure-mapping is an open alternative.
